evidence.detail: HEAD exactly matches the launcher-bound target commit. The working tree is clean.
The launcher-bound base-to-target diff contains 67 changed paths, principally replacing the vanilla frontend with React/Vite and adding associated tests and documentation.
Round-2 evidence records 174 Python tests passing, successful Python compilation and governance validation, successful TypeScript/Vite builds, and 88 Vitest tests passing against the candidate tree.
Independent Python execution ran 174 tests but 68 server tests could not bind loopback sockets under the read-only review sandbox. The remaining tests completed without reported failures.
Independent governance validation could not create a temporary directory because the review sandbox has no writable location.
Independent frontend tests could not start because the isolated checkout has no frontend/node_modules directory and installing dependencies is neither authorized nor possible in this review.

AuthManager.poll installs a token only while its original session remains current; logout clears every current authentication mode and retained app-only credential rather than conditionally clearing the abandoned handle.

The new regression test verifies that a logout request is issued, but its mock always succeeds and it does not verify cleanup completion, cleanup failure, or interaction with a newer authentication transition.

evidence: Expected: abandoning a device-code attempt must reliably remove only that attempt's server-side authentication state without disrupting a newer authentication transition.

Observed: after detecting a stale successful poll, pollOnce invokes `void authLogout()` without awaiting or checking it. A network/server failure silently leaves the orphaned token installed—the same high-impact condition this repair is intended to eliminate.

Observed: `/api/auth/logout` is unconditional and AuthManager.logout clears the current device session, access token, and retained app-only credentials. If an app-only or newer authentication transition completes after the stale poll installed its token but before the fire-and-forget logout is processed, this cleanup can erase the newer valid session.
The regression test only counts a mocked logout request whose response always succeeds; it cannot detect either failure mode.
findings.remediation: Make cancellation/cleanup ordered and attempt-specific. Prefer invalidating the server-side device session when the user abandons it, before beginning a competing authentication transition, with an awaited operation and explicit failure handling. Alternatively add a server API that conditionally clears only the named device attempt/generation. Do not use an unconditional fire-and-forget logout after another session may have become current.
findings.title: Stale-success cleanup is neither reliable nor scoped to the abandoned attempt
findings.verification: Add race/error tests showing: (1) cleanup failure cannot silently leave an unreachable authenticated server session; (2) switching to app-only authentication cannot be logged out by delayed cleanup from the abandoned device attempt; (3) starting a newer device attempt cannot be cleared by old cleanup; and (4) sample/sign-out transitions leave AuthManager unauthenticated. Run frontend and backend integration suites against the repaired commit.

limitations: The checkout is read-only and provides no writable temporary directory, so governance validation could not complete independently.
The sandbox prohibits loopback socket binding, preventing 68 of 174 Python tests from executing independently.
Frontend dependencies are absent, and this review was not authorized to install them; TypeScript build and Vitest results therefore rely on the commit-bound handoff evidence.
The manual browser walkthrough has no durable recording and was not independently reproducible.
Live Microsoft tenant authentication remains untested and is explicitly deferred as a protected action.
The repository is a shallow/grafted isolated checkout; target and base objects and their exact diff were available, but ordinary parent-range inspection was limited by the graft boundary.
review.summary: CHANGES_REQUIRED. The round-2 repair issues an unconditional, fire-and-forget logout after a stale successful poll. Cleanup failure can preserve the orphaned server token, while delayed cleanup can erase a newer valid session. The existing regression test proves only that a logout request was attempted. Commit-bound check evidence is present, but several checks could not be independently reproduced because of sandbox restrictions.
